## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Refresh must preserve stored fingerprints before merge because replacing them lets hand-edited tracked files pass verification.

## Changes

The pull request adds helpers to refresh fingerprints and register previously unlisted files. It adds tests for new files, unchanged tracked files, and empty input.

## Critical

- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — Preserve stored fingerprints during refresh — When `names` includes a tracked file that was edited by hand, refresh replaces its baseline with a digest of the edited bytes. `verify` compares the file against that replacement. — Refreshing after adding files can erase the evidence needed to detect edits to tracked content. — Fix: Reuse the existing-entry check in `register_new_files` and extend `test_refresh_registers_new_files_and_keeps_unchanged_entries`.

## Important

- app/integrity.py:25 — correctness — Exclude the manifest from its own entries — If a file list includes an unlisted `fingerprints.json` inside the content root, registration stores its digest and then rewrites it, invalidating that digest. Refresh uses the same read-then-write sequence. — Including the manifest in a directory-wide update makes verification fail even when every content file is intact.
